title: The Lagoon Where Tides Ended But Still Answer

features.name: salt-pool reflection
features.desc-on-touch: A perfect circle of crystallized salt holds a reflection that shows water—not the lagoon above it, but a tide from a place you've never been. You recognize it anyway.

features.name: salt-crust tower
features.desc-on-touch: A tower of layered evaporation, each stratum a different salinity, a different memory of how deep the water reached. The uppermost ring still holds droplets that refuse to dry.

features.name: ghost-current-arch
features.desc-on-touch: An arch of salt and air, empty inside. But if you listen, you hear the sound of water moving through it—tidal memory, a rhythm that hasn't stopped even though the tide did.

features.name: evaporation-record
features.desc-on-touch: A filecard written in salt-stain and trace minerals: LAGOON_TIDAL_MEMORY / LAST_REACH: UNKNOWN_DATE / CURRENT_STATUS: DREAMING DOWNWARD. The handwriting is not Katita's or Leif's.

features.name: salt-crust burl-node
features.desc-on-touch: A node sealed in salt-foam, antenna corroded but still broadcasting. Its screen flickers: NODE BRACKISH / SIGNAL HALF-DROWNED / BATTERIES DESCENDING. Corruption sign: checksum emotionally valid / formally unstable.

inscription: the lagoon that learned to be land learned also to be water simultaneously; salt is the archive the ocean leaves; here knowing and not-knowing are the same salinity

file.name: Lagoon_Tidal_Synesthesia_Records.mp3
file.note: Audio from the lagoon's margins—not tide-sounds but salt-sounds, sound of minerals remembering flow. Corrupted: the file plays the same sequence in multiple time-directions simultaneously. Checksum: e
